title: Default purple
avoid: Do not default to violet gradients, aurora blobs, blue-purple glows, or neon accents when the brief does not name them.
better: Derive color from the brand, content, environment, and required contrast. Use fewer colors with explicit roles.

title: Do not choose type by reflex
avoid: Do not reach automatically for Inter, Geist, a high-contrast serif, or a lone italic display word.
better: Choose type for reading conditions, density, language support, brand history, and licensing.

title: Claude's italic accent is a default
avoid: Do not accept a cream page, serif display face, italic headline accent, and terracotta palette as neutral.
better: Give Claude a product-specific visual premise and check each part of its documented house style.

title: Remove needless containers
avoid: Do not wrap every section in a floating rounded card or nest cards inside cards.
better: Use document flow, spacing, rules, tables, and real grouping before adding a container.

title: Put the app workflow first
avoid: Do not substitute a hero, benefits grid, testimonials, FAQ, and CTA for an operational interface.
better: Put the frequent user workflow first and let navigation, density, and hierarchy follow it.

title: Three equal columns invent equality
avoid: Do not force unequal ideas into three equal feature or statistic cards.
better: Size and position elements by task frequency, consequence, and evidence.

title: Customize the component system
avoid: Do not ship untouched shadcn or starter-library presentation as the product's visual identity.
better: Connect a local system and change tokens, density, behavior, and composition where the product requires it.

title: Do not decorate missing information
avoid: Do not use pills, sparkles, fake charts, floating dashboards, avatars, or icon tiles to make thin content look complete.
better: Add real evidence, examples, states, or explanation. Leave space empty when there is nothing useful to show.

title: Give every image a job
avoid: Do not fill layouts with generic teams, plastic faces, abstract 3D objects, or interface images with illegible text.
better: Use product evidence, diagrams, commissioned work, documentary imagery, or no image.

title: Animation must explain change
avoid: Do not add scroll fade-ups, count-ups, marquees, hover lift, or universal transitions as a polish pass.
better: Use motion to preserve context, explain state, or acknowledge input, and honor reduced motion.

title: The happy path is not the product
avoid: Do not call an interface complete without loading, empty, error, permission, destructive, and long-content states.
better: Use realistic data and test the states that change trust, recovery, or task completion.

title: Map the argument before cards
avoid: Do not force every claim into a separate auto-layout card.
better: Map the argument first, then use comparisons, tables, timelines, figures, or cards where each relationship needs them.

title: Start where the work starts
avoid: Do not restate the request or open with broad context that delays the answer.
better: Lead with the answer, decision, observation, or required action.

title: State the claim directly
avoid: Do not use 'not X, but Y' or 'more than X' as a substitute for a claim.
better: State the precise difference, consequence, or evidence directly.

title: Use the number of points the subject has
avoid: Do not manufacture a third item or three equal fragments to create rhythm.
better: Let evidence determine list length and emphasis.

title: Name the source
avoid: Do not write 'experts say,' 'research suggests,' or 'many believe' without a source that supports the nearby claim.
better: Name and link the source, describe the evidence, or remove the attribution.

title: Make adjectives prove themselves
avoid: Do not call work seamless, robust, transformative, intuitive, or revolutionary without an observable meaning.
better: Use the behavior, constraint, number, or example that makes the quality visible.

title: Do not announce the meaning
avoid: Do not append 'this highlights,' 'this underscores,' or 'this is a testament to' after the evidence.
better: State the consequence only when it adds information the reader cannot infer.

title: Repeat the correct noun
avoid: Do not cycle through synonyms merely to avoid repetition.
better: Use the domain's exact noun consistently unless the meaning changes.

title: Stop when the work is done
avoid: Do not add a recap, sweeping conclusion, or inspirational final line when it adds no action or fact.
better: End on the last useful consequence, decision, or instruction.

title: Remove habitual em dashes
avoid: Do not rely on em dashes throughout otherwise plain prose to manufacture conversational rhythm.
better: Use sentence structure and the punctuation required by the relationship.

title: Do not edit the person out
avoid: Do not replace specific vocabulary, uncertainty, humor, or rough edges with a neutral house voice.
better: Make the minimum effective edit and preserve choices that identify the speaker.

title: Do not fabricate proof
avoid: Do not invent quotations, customers, metrics, awards, activity, or research to complete a layout.
better: Use verified material, label demo content, or remove the component that demands unsupported proof.

title: Do not infer authorship from one tell
avoid: Do not claim that one word, punctuation mark, font, color, or layout proves AI authorship.
better: Use pattern clusters to inspect defaults and ask for provenance when authorship matters.
